## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Assessing Our Results
■ What are the trends over time?
■ What are the trends for groups?

■ How did overall achievement change,

compared to the same students’ achievement
last year?
■ How does the change compare to a standards-

based or norms-based idea of a year’s growth?
■ How does the change differ by groups?

■ How do achievement data compare with school

climate, parent, staff and NCG survey results?</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Colorado Student Assessment Program

•Grades 3-10 Read/Write/Math; Sci at 5,8,10
•Based on Content Standards
•Standardized Administration to Nearly All
Students, with Accommodations Available
•Selected- and Open-Response Questions
•CSAP Development Process and Statistical
Evidence Support Making Inferences from
Results
•Growth Data More Relevant for Many
Purposes than Achievement</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">A Relatively New Metric: Colorado’s Growth
Model

■ Easier to use and understand than
the previous methods
■ Supported by a useful video

■ CDE graphs available online by

district and school
■ Current year results arrived at a later

than ideal time for full use</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Colorado Median Growth Percentile
■ Amount of gain is statistically compared
across students starting from the same
point (“academic peers”)
■ Growth percentile assigned: percent of

“academic peers” making that amount of
gain or less
■ Percentiles range from 1 to 99, can be

compared with state median of 50
■ Accountability Measure: the middle growth

%-ile</div>
```

::: notes
```{=html}
Bullet 2 --- Norm based model<br>
Bullet 4 --- 50 is typical for a state-wide interpretation
```
:::

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/13.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Productive Response to Median
Growth Percentile
■ Users are far less dismissive of gaps
in growth than in achievement
■ Because a student’s growth is not

readily predicted, raising median
growth requires group improvement
■ Reflection on what went well for

students with high growth</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/14.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">School and Teacher Use
■ Fair comparison across content
areas
■ Encouraged for use in school goal

setting, especially around equity
■ Published at student level in Student

Information System (Infinite
Campus), contextualized with
grades, demographics, simple gain</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/18.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Avoiding Over-Interpretation

■ Contextualize with Error Estimates
■ Examine Multiple Content Areas

and Years of Results for Each
Student
■ Consider Likely Response of

Parents, Having Seen Percentiles
only for Achievement, not Growth</div>
```
